name: Naqshbandiyya
dom: silent dhikr; sober Sufism; sharia-bound spirituality; the Khwajagan lineage
note: Major Sunni Sufi tariqa traced to Baha al-Din Naqshband, distinguished by silent dhikr (dhikr-i khafi) and tracing its silsila to Abu Bakr.

name: Chishtiyya
dom: sama (audition); service to the poor; love of God; South Asian Sufism
note: Sufi order rooted in Chisht (Afghanistan) and established in India by Mu'in al-Din Chishti, central to the Islamization of the subcontinent.

name: Bektashiyya
dom: Anatolian heterodoxy; Alevi devotion; veneration of Ali; antinomian piety
note: Heterodox Anatolian Sufi order traced to Hajji Bektash Wali, later linked to the Janissaries and to Alevi communities.

name: Ni'matullahiyya
dom: Persian Sufism; wahdat al-wujud; poetry and devotion
note: Persian Sufi order founded by Shah Ni'matullah Wali, the most widespread tariqa in Iran.

name: Kubrawiyya
dom: visionary mysticism; colours of the soul; Central Asian Sufism
note: Central Asian Sufi order founded by Najm al-Din Kubra, noted for its visionary psychology of luminous colours.

name: Badawiyya
dom: Egyptian popular Sufism; saint-veneration; the Tanta mawlid
note: Egyptian Sufi order centred on the shrine of Ahmad al-Badawi at Tanta, host to one of the largest mawlid festivals in Islam.

name: Najm al-Din Kubra
dom: visionary mysticism; spiritual psychology; sainthood
note: Persian mystic (d. 1221), eponymous founder of the Kubrawiyya; martyred at the Mongol sack of Khwarazm. Author of works on the visionary lights of the soul.

name: Sadr al-Din al-Qunawi
dom: metaphysics; wahdat al-wujud; theology of unveiling
note: Persian-Anatolian metaphysician (d. 1274), stepson and chief successor of Ibn al-Arabi who systematized his teaching of the oneness of being.

name: Fakhr al-Din Iraqi
dom: mystical love-poetry; wahdat al-wujud; divine beauty
note: Persian Sufi poet (d. 1289), disciple of Qunawi's circle, whose Lama'at expounds Ibn al-Arabi's doctrine through the imagery of love.

name: Awhad al-Din Kirmani
dom: contemplation of divine beauty; quatrains; the witness (shahid)
note: Persian Sufi master and poet (d. 1238) known for the contemplation of divine beauty in created forms (shahid-bazi) and for his ruba'iyat.

name: Mu'in al-Din Chishti
dom: sainthood; service to the poor; conversion; Indian Sufism
note: Persian saint (d. 1236) who established the Chishtiyya in India; his shrine (dargah) at Ajmer is among the most venerated in South Asia. Titled Gharib Nawaz.

name: Qutb al-Din Bakhtiar Kaki
dom: sainthood; sama; the Delhi Chishti line
note: Chishti saint of Delhi (d. 1235), foremost disciple of Mu'in al-Din Chishti; his shrine at Mehrauli anchors the Delhi Chishti tradition.

name: Farid al-Din Ganj-i-Shakar
dom: asceticism; Punjabi devotion; sainthood
note: Punjabi Chishti saint (d. 1265), 'Baba Farid'; his verses are included in the Sikh Guru Granth Sahib. Shrine at Pakpattan.

name: Nizam al-Din Awliya
dom: sainthood; love and tolerance; Delhi Sultanate Sufism
note: Pre-eminent Chishti saint of Delhi (d. 1325), 'Mahbub-i Ilahi'; his dargah is a major South Asian pilgrimage centre.

name: Amir Khusrow
dom: Persian and Hindavi poetry; qawwali; devotion to the master
note: Indo-Persian poet and musician (d. 1325), devoted disciple of Nizam al-Din Awliya and a father of the qawwali devotional song.

name: Baha al-Din Naqshband
dom: silent dhikr; sober Sufism; the Khwajagan path
note: Central Asian saint of Bukhara (d. 1389), eponym of the Naqshbandiyya, who emphasized silent remembrance and presence in the world.

name: Khwaja Ubayd Allah Ahrar
dom: sainthood; political influence; Naqshbandi consolidation
note: Naqshbandi master of Samarqand (d. 1490) who gave the order great political and economic weight under the Timurids.

name: Ahmad al-Badawi
dom: Egyptian popular sainthood; miracle-working; the Tanta mawlid
note: Saint of Tanta (d. 1276), eponym of the Badawiyya and one of the most popular saints of Egypt.

name: Ibrahim al-Dasuqi
dom: Egyptian sainthood; the four 'aqtab'; devotion
note: Egyptian saint (d. 1296), eponym of the Dasuqiyya (Burhaniyya) and counted among the four great qutbs of Egyptian Sufism.

name: Shah Ni'matullah Wali
dom: Persian sainthood; mystical poetry; wahdat al-wujud
note: Persian saint and poet (d. 1431), founder of the Ni'matullahi order; his shrine at Mahan is a major Iranian pilgrimage site.

name: Hajji Bektash Wali
dom: Anatolian sainthood; antinomian piety; veneration of Ali
note: Anatolian saint (d. 1271) revered as the founder-patron of the Bektashiyya and of Alevi devotion.

name: Yunus Emre
dom: Turkish devotional poetry; divine love; folk mysticism
note: Turkish saint-poet (d. 1321), father of Turkish-language Sufi poetry whose hymns of divine love remain central to Anatolian devotion.

name: Hafiz of Shiraz
dom: Persian ghazal; mystical love and wine; divine beauty
note: Persian lyric poet (d. 1390), 'Lisan al-Ghayb', whose ghazals fuse the imagery of love and wine with mystical longing; venerated and used for bibliomancy (fal).

name: Mahmud Shabistari
dom: mystical metaphysics; wahdat al-wujud; symbolic exegesis
note: Persian Sufi poet (d. 1340) whose Gulshan-i Raz (Rose Garden of Mystery) is a classic verse summary of Ibn al-Arabi's metaphysics.

name: Abd al-Karim al-Jili
dom: metaphysics; the Perfect Man (al-insan al-kamil); wahdat al-wujud
note: Yemeni-Iraqi mystic (d. c. 1424) whose al-Insan al-Kamil developed Ibn al-Arabi's doctrine of the Perfect Man.

name: Safi al-Din Ardabili
dom: sainthood; the Safavid order; Azerbaijani Sufism
note: Persian saint of Ardabil (d. 1334), eponym of the Safaviyya order from which the Safavid dynasty later arose.

name: Sayyid Ali Hamadani
dom: missionary sainthood; Kubrawi path; Kashmiri Sufism
note: Persian Kubrawi saint (d. 1385) credited with spreading Islam and Persianate culture in Kashmir; 'Shah-i Hamadan'.

name: Sharaf al-Din Maneri
dom: sainthood; spiritual letters; Firdausi-Suhrawardi path
note: Indian Sufi master of Bihar (d. 1381) of the Firdausiyya (a Suhrawardi branch), famed for his Maktubat (Hundred Letters) of spiritual counsel.

name: Lal Ded
dom: Kashmiri mystical verse; non-dual devotion; the rishi tradition
note: Kashmiri mystic poet (d. c. 1392), 'Lalla', whose vakhs voice a non-dual devotion bridging Shaiva and Sufi piety; revered by Hindus and Muslims alike.

name: Nur al-Din Nurani
dom: Kashmiri sainthood; the Rishi order; asceticism
note: Kashmiri saint (d. c. 1440), 'Nund Rishi', patron-founder of the Kashmiri Rishi order; venerated as Alamdar-i Kashmir.

name: Abd al-Rahman Jami
dom: Persian poetry; Naqshbandi devotion; hagiography; wahdat al-wujud
note: Persian poet and Naqshbandi mystic (d. 1492), last of the great classical Persian poets; his Nafahat al-Uns is a major saints' hagiography.
